s1.syndrome_frame: Acute cardiac syndrome with respiratory distress and hemodynamic instability
salient_findings: Severe left ventricular dysfunction on echocardiography
key_facts: Patient presented with chest pain and dyspnea
Patient had symptoms of upper respiratory tract infection 3 days prior
Vital signs: temperature 36.5°C, heart rate 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate 22 breaths per minute, blood pressure 105/70 mm Hg, oxygen saturation 89% on room air
Patient lost consciousness 20 minutes after arrival
Blood pressure decreased to 67/43 mm Hg after loss of consciousness
Troponin T level was 4.74 μg/L
Pro-brain natriuretic peptide level was 4850 pg/mL
C-reactive protein level was 18.50 mg/L
Procalcitonin level was 39.68 ng/mL
Transthoracic echocardiography showed severe left ventricular dysfunction with ejection fraction 38%
Coronary angiography showed normal coronary arteries
Initial ECG showed upward QRS complex in lead aVR and pure R wave in leads V1 and V2
Follow-up ECG showed sinus tachycardia, low QRS voltage in limb leads, ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, aVF, and V1-V6, and ST-segment depression in leads aVR and aVL

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had symptoms of upper respiratory tract infection 3 days prior and presented with chest pain, dyspnea, and severe left ventricular dysfunction

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin T level and ST-segment elevation in multiple leads on ECG

shortlist.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with chest pain, dyspnea, and severe left ventricular dysfunction, but coronary angiography showed normal coronary arteries

shortlist.label: Myopericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had symptoms of upper respiratory tract infection 3 days prior and presented with chest pain, dyspnea, and ST-segment elevation in multiple leads on ECG

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with chest pain, dyspnea, and severe left ventricular dysfunction, but coronary angiography showed normal coronary arteries and patient had a significant decrease in blood pressure

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with chest pain, dyspnea, and symptoms of upper respiratory tract infection, along with elevated troponin T, pro-brain natriuretic peptide, C-reactive protein, and procalcitonin levels, suggests an inflammatory process. The transthoracic echocardiography showing severe left ventricular dysfunction and the follow-up ECG changes are also consistent with myocarditis. The normal coronary angiography rules out acute myocardial infarction due to coronary artery occlusion.

rejected.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: Lack of clear stressor and different ECG pattern

rejected.label: Myopericarditis
rejected.why: Echocardiography did not show pericardial involvement

rejected.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: ECG and echocardiography findings not typical for this condition
